blocks.title: Relative masses and the mole
blocks.md: Relative atomic masses (A_r): H 1, C 12, N 14, O 16, Na 23, Mg 24, Al 27, S 32, Cl 35.5, K 39, Ca 40, Fe 56, Cu 64, Zn 65. The **relative formula mass (M_r)** is the sum of the A_r values: M_r(H₂SO₄) = 2 + 32 + 64 = **98**. The **mole** is the amount of substance containing **6.0 × 10²³** particles (the Avogadro constant, more exactly 6.02 × 10²³). The **molar mass M** is the mass of one mole in **g/mol** and equals the M_r (or A_r) in grams.

items.text: m = n × M     n = m ÷ M     M = m ÷ n
m: mass in g,  n: moles,  M: molar mass in g/mol

blocks.caption: The mole triangle: cover the quantity you want.
blocks.alt: A triangle divided into three parts with m at the top and n and M at the bottom, with the three formulae m = n × M, n = m ÷ M and M = m ÷ n.

blocks.title: Calculations
blocks.md: **n = m ÷ M**, **m = n × M**; number of particles = **n × 6.0 × 10²³**. **Percentage by mass of an element** = (A_r × number of atoms ÷ M_r) × 100. **Empirical formula** (simplest ratio of atoms): (1) write the masses or percentages; (2) divide each by its A_r; (3) divide by the smallest; (4) round to whole numbers. Example: 2.4 g Mg and 1.6 g O → 0.1 mol and 0.1 mol → ratio 1 : 1 → **MgO**.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Use the **M_r of the whole formula**: for CaCO₃ it is 40 + 12 + 48 = 100.
- A bracket multiplies: M_r of Ca(OH)₂ is 40 + 2 × (16 + 1) = 74.
- The empirical formula is a ratio, not the true number of atoms: the molecular formula may be a multiple of it (CH₂ for C₂H₄).

lessons.title: Reacting masses, gas volumes and concentration
lessons.programRef: Form 4 Chemistry — Relative masses, the mole, reacting masses and volumes (to be checked)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Use balanced equations to calculate reacting masses and gas volumes.
Calculate concentration and carry out a titration calculation.
reviewNotes: Molar volume 24 dm³/mol at r.t.p. (some syllabuses use 22.4 dm³ at s.t.p.); check which one the syllabus uses. All numerical answers were recomputed in the generator with assertions.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Mass and volume calculations
blocks.md:
1. Write the **balanced equation**.
2. Convert the known mass to **moles** (n = m ÷ M).
3. Use the **mole ratio** from the equation.
4. Convert the moles of the wanted substance to **mass** (n × M) or **gas volume** (n × 24 dm³ at room temperature and pressure; the molar volume of a gas is **24 dm³/mol** at r.t.p.).

blocks.title: Concentration and titration
blocks.md: **Concentration (mol/dm³) c = n ÷ V** (V in dm³; 1 dm³ = 1000 cm³), so **n = c × V**. Concentration in g/dm³ = c × M. In a **titration** a **burette** adds acid to a measured volume of alkali in a flask with an indicator until it just changes colour (the **end-point**, read to 0.05 cm³); repeat until two results agree within 0.10 cm³ (**concordant**).

items.text: start reading 0.0 cm³, end reading 20.0 cm³

blocks.caption: A titration set-up.
blocks.alt: A burette of acid above a conical flask containing alkali and indicator standing on a white tile, with the note start reading 0.0 cm³ and end reading 20.0 cm³.

blocks.title: Percentage yield
blocks.md: **Percentage yield = (actual mass obtained ÷ theoretical mass) × 100**. The yield is below 100 % because of incomplete reactions, losses when filtering and transferring and side reactions.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Convert cm³ to dm³ **before** using c = n ÷ V: 25 cm³ = 0.025 dm³.
- Use the **mole ratio**, not the mass ratio, from the equation.
- Use 24 dm³/mol only for gases at room temperature and pressure.

blocks.title: Reacting mass
blocks.statement: 4.8 g of magnesium burns completely in oxygen. Find the mass of magnesium oxide formed (2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO; A_r: Mg 24, O 16).
steps: n(Mg) = 4.8 ÷ 24 = 0.20 mol; ratio Mg : MgO = 1 : 1, so 0.20 mol MgO.

blocks.title: Titration
blocks.statement: 25.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol/dm³ NaOH needs 20.0 cm³ of HCl for neutralisation. Find the concentration of the acid (NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O).
